"Create a 3D game inspired by Agentic Wars: Conquest with aTERRA HEXA — 3D WORLD BUILDING GAME

Create a complete, playable mobile game called TERRA HEXA, a colorful 3D isometric world-building and simulation game.

VISUAL STYLE

Create a beautiful, vibrant low-poly 3D world inspired by miniature diorama games. Use colorful environments, turquoise water, lush forests, pink flowering trees, modern houses, farms, futuristic buildings, animals, tiny characters, waterfalls, boats, and animated nature.

Use a clean, elegant mobile interface with soft green, turquoise, cream, and white colors.

GAME STRUCTURE

Preserve a portrait mobile layout with:

- A central interactive 3D hexagonal world.
- Player avatar, level, experience, coins, stars, and resources at the top.
- Camera controls on the sides.
- A tile selection panel at the bottom.
- A separate main menu with the game logo, player progress, world preview, and a Continue button.

HEXAGONAL TILE SYSTEM

Create six main tile types: Field, Forest, Water, Farm, Coast, and Mountain.

Players must place, rotate, remove, and connect tiles to expand their world.

Implement universal automatic edge matching so compatible tiles fit together perfectly like puzzle pieces, without gaps, overlaps, or disconnected surfaces. Water, farms, forests, roads, beaches, and mountains must connect naturally.

RESOURCES AND ECONOMY

Allow players to collect wood, stone, water, fish, wheat, vegetables, fruits, flowers, clay, and minerals directly from the world.

Resources must regenerate over time.

Create a functional economy where resources are spent on:

- Constructing houses, farms, bridges, markets, warehouses, and production buildings.
- Producing materials and food.
- Upgrading buildings.
- Expanding the territory.
- Unlocking new biomes and structures.

Include farming, planting, crop growth, harvesting, crafting, production timers, inventory, storage, and a marketplace where players buy and sell resources.

LIVING WORLD

Make the world feel alive with animated villagers, farmers, animals, birds, fish, moving boats, flowing water, waterfalls, windmills, trees moving in the wind, and a day/night cycle.

Population should grow as settlements develop.

PROGRESSION

Add player levels, experience, missions, achievements, rewards, new buildings, new tiles, and unlockable biomes.

Players should always have new goals to complete and new areas to explore.

INTERFACE AND SAVE SYSTEM

Support Portuguese (Brazil) and English.

Add functional settings, sound controls, and smooth mobile touch interactions.

Save all progress, including tiles, buildings, resources, inventory, levels, and production.

FINAL REQUIREMENT

Create a fully functional and playable game, not just a visual prototype.

Prioritize the hexagonal puzzle connection system, resource collection, construction, economy, and a beautiful living 3D world.

Preserve mobile performance and ensure every button and gameplay mechanic actually works.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build TERRA HEXA, a complete playable mobile 3D isometric world-building game inspired by Agentic Wars: Conquest, in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Portrait-friendly colorful low-poly 3D world, with a central hex world, progress/resources, camera controls, tile selector, and separate welcome/menu screen.
- Six hex tile types: Field, Forest, Water, Farm, Coast, Mountain; support placement, rotation, removal, expansion, and natural connections.
- Functional resource collection and regeneration, construction, economy/trading, inventory, missions/progression, living-world animation, save system, settings, and English/Portuguese (Brazil).
- Mobile touch interactions and performance; buttons and mechanics should work.
- User asked to build immediately without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a browser game using Three.js from a CDN, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and `localStorage` persistence.
- Used procedural low-poly geometry and emoji/icon UI instead of external model assets.
- Made reasonable scope tradeoffs for a single-file prototype: core tile/resource/build/trade loops and animated diorama first.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with the game HUD, resource rail, tile selector, camera buttons, modal root, and welcome overlay.
- Created `styles.css` with responsive mobile layout, polished UI, and modal styling.
- Started implementing Three.js world rendering and core game state in `game.js`; added procedural tiles, props, buildings, characters, birds, boat, tile hit testing, hover preview, and world rebuilding.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest replacement of `game.js`.

- `game.js` is incomplete: the latest write ended after `onMove()` and currently lacks pointer click handling, gameplay actions, HUD updates, modals, persistence completion, UI event binding, and game initialization.

3. Start the project using its configured launch workflow, inspect the browser experience and fix visual/functionality issues.
4. Report implemented scope and any remaining assumptions/limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game UI markup.
- `styles.css`: game visual styling and mobile layout.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene and game logic; currently incomplete.

- Build TERRA HEXA, a playable mobile 3D isometric world-building game in the existing project.
- Finish and validate the game experience, including its world interactions, economy, progression, settings, and save system.

- Portrait-friendly colorful low-poly 3D world, HUD, tile selector, camera controls, and separate welcome screen.

- Functional resources, construction, trading, inventory, missions/progression, animation, saving, settings, and English/Portuguese (Brazil).
- Mobile touch interactions and functional controls; build without clarification.

- Browser game using Three.js from a CDN, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, `localStorage`, and procedural low-poly geometry.
- Core interactions and polished diorama are prioritized for the prototype.

## Objective
- Complete TERRA HEXA as a playable, portrait-friendly 3D world-building game, then validate its core experience and controls.

## Requirements
- Six placeable tile types; world expansion and removal; resources, buildings, trading, missions, progression, settings, and local saves.
- Mobile-friendly controls, English and Brazilian Portuguese, and a separate welcome screen.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js via CDN, procedural low-poly geometry, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Finished `game.js` UI wiring for tile selection, construction, removal, gathering, market, missions, inventory, settings, language switching, welcome screen, and save/reset actions.
- Added modal styling to `styles.css` to support the new game modal markup.
- Fixed save loading to preserve the default starting buildings when no buildings are saved.
- `node --check game.js` passed; served the app at `http://localhost:3000` and verified the Three.js canvas, welcome overlay dismissal, six tile options, and settings modal in Chromium.

### Active
- Validate gameplay interactions and inspect the active-world presentation; a follow-up screenshot capture attempt failed before saving.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli open` could not run because its expected Chromium installation is missing; system Chromium and Chrome DevTools Protocol were used instead.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser validation of tile placement, building, gathering, market, missions, and persistence.
2. Inspect an active-world screenshot and fix any visual or interaction issues.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js` after any changes and summarize remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, UI wiring, state, and initialization.
- `index.html`: Game HUD, welcome overlay, and modal root.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and modal presentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status.
- The server was started with `bash start.sh` on port 3000.
- The initial screenshot at `/tmp/terra-hexa.png` was captured before dismissing the welcome overlay; the later active-world screenshot attempt failed with a Node module-format error.
